To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coarse grained free energy functional of the hard-core interacting system is given by a functional that is a convex combination of the free energy functional of a noninteracting system and the free energy functional that arises in the case of short-range repulsive interactions.

we have identified a new type of macroscopic Fokker–Plank equations that arise from the coarse graining of a microscopic model with excluded volume effects, that the macroscopic equations preserve the gradient structure of the microscopic ones, and that the free-energy functionals of both the microscopic and macroscopic models are explicitly known.

we have derived a macroscopic gradient flow for the diffusion of a large number of particles interacting by hard-core exclusion or a short-range potential, which is the first derivation of such a macroscopic gradient for a system of particles interacting by volume exclusion, which is the only known derivation of such a gradient for a system that does not assume that the particles are small compared to the domain, and which shows how the gradient structure of the microscopic model is transferred to the macroscopic model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the correct notions of gradient structure for the macroscopic model and for the microscopic model? How do these structures relate to each other?
the propagation of gradient flows from microscopic models to their coarse-grained versions.

the following questions: (i) What is the macroscopic free energy functional for the diffusion of hard-core interacting particles? (ii) What is the corresponding Wasserstein metric on the space of probability measures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the limit of vanishing volume, the macroscopic gradient flow structure emerges from a microscopic one in a very precise way.
the macroscopic model for the coarse-grained system can be obtained as the limit of the microscopic model by a propagation of the gradient structure.
the macroscopic gradient flow structure is preserved, but the free energy functional is modified due to the volume effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the macroscopic gradient structure is robust with respect to small particle interactions, but it is modified by the excluded volume effects.
the macroscopic free-energy functional is given by the sum of a non-local free-energy functional for single particle densities and a local free-energy density functional for two particle densities.

the gradient structure of a microscopic system is propagated to the macroscopic level in an asymptotic limit, but the macroscopic free energy functional contains corrections due to the excluded volume effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the macroscopic gradient flow structure is preserved in the limit, and that the corrections to the free energy functional can be expressed as a functional of the macroscopic density.
the macroscopic gradient structure can be identified by a simple scaling of the microscopic free energy.

the macroscopic free-energy functional can be obtained by coarse graining of the microscopic one, but that the coarse graining is nontrivial and requires the consideration of correlations at small distances.
